Playbook.name: AD — Kerberos Brute Force Against a Single Account (4771 bad-password burst) - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: 20 or more Kerberos pre-auth failures with status 0x18 (bad password) hit ONE account within 30 minutes. Triage question: is one entity guessing this account's password, or does the account have a stale saved credential (Outlook/mobile/service) hammering the DC?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: A guessed account yields domain credentials; in JCB several human accounts (e.g. stale-credential patterns) generate the same shape, so the distinction drives whether this is IR or helpdesk.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security auditing shipped via Elastic Agent to logs-system.security-* (verified live).

Signal.Name: Per-account 0x18 burst
Signal.Details: >= 20 KRB pre-auth failures, status 0x18, one TargetUserName, machine accounts excluded.

Input.name: $target_user
Input.description: The account under attack (threshold group key from the alert).

InitialAssessment.Rule: Stale credential pattern: same single source host, evenly spaced failures continuing for days - lean Misconfiguration.
Guessing pattern: new/unknown source, tight burst, possibly followed by lockout or success - escalate.

Investigation.Goal: Decide whether $target_user is being actively guessed, has a stale stored credential, or was compromised (success after burst).

Step.name: Locate the failure sources and cadence for this account
Step.Purpose: Identify WHERE the failures come from and whether the cadence is machine-regular or attack-bursty.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code == "4771" AND winlog.event_data.TargetUserName == "$target_user" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | EVAL src = COALESCE(TO_STRING(source.ip), "local/unknown") | STATS fails = COUNT(*), first_seen = MIN(@timestamp), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp), statuses = VALUES(winlog.event_data.Status), dcs = VALUES(host.name) BY src | SORT fails DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: One workstation IP with steady failures over hours/days = stale credential on that device. Multiple sources or a new source with a tight burst = guessing. Status 0x12 mixed in = account got locked/disabled during the burst.

Step.name: Did the account authenticate successfully afterwards, and from where
Step.Purpose: Success from the SAME source as the failures = likely compromise; success from the user's normal workstation = user recovered/changed password.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code == "4624" AND winlog.event_data.TargetUserName == "$target_user" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | EVAL src = COALESCE(TO_STRING(source.ip), "local") | STATS logons = COUNT(*), first_success = MIN(@timestamp), types = VALUES(winlog.event_data.LogonType), hosts = VALUES(host.name) BY src | SORT first_success ASC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: Match src against INV-01 sources. Success from the failing source shortly after the burst is the key TP indicator. LogonType 2/10 from a NEW source is worse than type 3 service traffic.

Step.name: Was the account locked out or disabled during the window
Step.Purpose: Lockout (4740) confirms threshold pressure and gives the caller computer; a disable (4725) may be the SOC/IT response already in motion.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code IN ("4740","4725","4722") AND winlog.event_data.TargetUserName == "$target_user" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | KEEP @timestamp, event.code, winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName, host.name | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 10
Step.AnalystNotes: 4740 = lockout occurred. Repeated lock/unlock cycles (4740 then 4722) with continuing failures = unattended credential loop still running.

Node.Condition: INV-02 shows a success from the same source that produced the INV-01 failure burst, within the window.
Node.Result: True Positive (Likely Account Compromise - escalate to IR)

Node.Condition: INV-01 shows a new or unowned source with a tight burst (20+ in minutes) and no prior history pattern, regardless of success.

INV-01 shows one known workstation/device steadily failing for hours-days with identical 0x18, INV-02 successes only from the user's normal source, INV-03 may show repeated lockouts (JCB stale-credential pattern, e.g. MohammadSw/ihamad class).
The account is a service account failing from its own application server continuously.
Sources are mixed or unidentifiable and no ownership can be established.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-KRB-SOURCES, INV-02-KRB-SUCCESS, INV-03-KRB-LOCKOUT to the case.

FalsePositive.Definition: Rare here: a legitimate bulk process (migration, SSO re-enrolment) causing a one-off burst for this account with a documented change.

Indicators.Item: Burst coincides exactly with a documented migration/re-enrolment activity.

SOCAction.Item: Close as false_positive; no tuning needed (one-off).

TruePositive.Definition: An entity is actively guessing this specific account's password (or already got in).

Indicators.Item: Tight burst from a source that is not the user's device.

SOCAction.Item: Reset the account password and revoke sessions/tickets.
Check the account's group membership - privileged targets escalate priority.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A stale stored credential (Outlook profile, mobile device, mapped drive, scheduled task, service) retrying forever.

Indicators.Item: Recurring lockouts for the same account (achuser pattern: ~95 lockouts/day).

SOCAction.Item: Helpdesk: locate and update the stored credential on the source device.
If a service account: fix the service credential; track under credential-hygiene P0.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: If success-after-burst: reset password + revoke sessions NOW.
Identify and notify the account owner.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Contain guessing source; verify no other accounts targeted from it (pivot to PB-AD-001 logic).

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Push MFA/conditional protections for repeatedly-targeted accounts.
Close the stale-credential loop via helpdesk ticket.

QualityChecks.Check: Suppression is 6h per account - repeated alerts for the SAME account on consecutive days indicates the loop was not fixed.
This rule sees only 0x18; disabled-account probing (0x12) is PB-AD-003.

FalsePositiveClosure.Item: Stale-credential source device identified and helpdesk ticket opened.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Password reset + ticket revocation done; source contained; IR notes recorded.
